comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C7, C73, C74, C119, C120 regarding challenges to local feedback theory. However, OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature of the proposed global hydromechanical mechanism, while peer reviewers rate it as SUPPORTED, accepting the challenge to local feedback theory and the possibility of alternative coupling mechanisms.

Perfect agreement on claims C92-C100 regarding inner hair cell stimulation mechanisms. Both evaluations agree these mechanisms are speculative and based on cited in vitro studies rather than direct measurement. Both rate as UNCERTAIN, with OpenEval noting authors acknowledge limitations (C100) and peer reviewers requesting discussion while acknowledging mechanisms 'remain to be determined experimentally.'

Strong agreement on claims C15-C23, C26-C28 regarding magnitude differences between reticular lamina and basilar membrane. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative measurements and nonlinear compression, while peer reviewers acknowledge the order of magnitude difference as an established finding without concerns.

Strong agreement on claims C32-C42, C63-C65 regarding postmortem control experiments demonstrating metabolic dependence. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights systematic changes and reversal of displacement direction as compelling evidence, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the postmortem data by focusing on requesting mechanistic discussion rather than challenging observations.

Strong agreement on claims C101-C106, C109 regarding mechanisms for latency differences. Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are speculative and based on inference from anatomical knowledge, while peer reviewers request discussion of coupling via Deiters' cell soma, indicating plausible but unconfirmed mechanisms.

Agreement on claims C122-C129 regarding methodological details. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes heterodyne interferometry addressing phase ambiguity and experimental rigor, while peer reviewers state 'the data are robust' and only request clarification about Figure 6 frequency rather than challenging validity.

Agreement on claims C52, C53, C111 regarding species differences. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes statistical support for species comparison while finding mechanical coupling speculation less well-supported, while peer reviewers accept observed species differences and request more interpretation without challenging the data.

Agreement on claims C4, C29-C31, C46-C47, C51, C59, C66, C117 regarding temporal relationships. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from frequency-domain and time-domain measurements with internal consistency, while peer reviewers explicitly state 'the data are robust and this is a significant finding' regarding the 20-30 microsecond timing.

Agreement on claims C81-C86 regarding longitudinal fluid movement mechanisms. Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes mechanistic interpretation is speculative and inferred rather than directly measured, while peer reviewers indicate this was covered in previous work and should be largely removed, suggesting it remains speculative rather than definitively established.

Partial overlap on claims C6, C47, C61, C67, C118 regarding in-phase relationships and constructive interference. OpenEval R1 rates temporal relationships as SUPPORTED focusing on phase measurements, while peer R3 rates in-phase relationship near best frequency as SUPPORTED and explicitly requests discussion of constructive/destructive interference implications.

Partial overlap on claims C5, C54-C55, C61 regarding opposite-direction movements. OpenEval R1 rates temporal relationships as SUPPORTED including click responses, while peer R2 rates opposite-direction findings as SUPPORTED, treating them as established results consistent with prior work on outer hair cell electromotility.

Minimal overlap on claims C49-C50 regarding sound level independence. OpenEval R7 rates as SUPPORTED with statistical validation, while peer R1 includes C49-C50 in broader temporal relationship evaluation rated as SUPPORTED without specific comment on sound level independence.

Minimal overlap on claim C113 regarding frequency-dependent interpretation. OpenEval R10 rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing reconciliation with in vitro observations, while peer R2 includes C113 in opposite-direction findings rated as SUPPORTED without specific comment on frequency dependence.

Minimal overlap on claim C115 regarding coherent framework. OpenEval R10 rates as SUPPORTED for providing coherent framework reconciling findings, while peer R3 includes C115 in in-phase relationship evaluation rated as SUPPORTED with focus on constructive interference implications.

OpenEval R8 addresses claims C68-C70 regarding comparison with prior literature (heterodyne vs. homodyne methods, species differences), rated as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing literature comparison methodology.

Peer R8 addresses claims C88-C90 regarding two-tone suppression and low frequency regions, rated as SUPPORTED with request for discussion. No corresponding OpenEval result found specifically evaluating these claims about two-tone suppression implications.
